memory_update.text: For grid_services_epc_labor, keep PWR as the high-attention reference benchmark, not the main alpha target.
MYRG is a direct mid-cap specialty electrical contractor candidate with transmission, distribution, substation, and electrification backlog relevance.
PRIM is a mixed-label infrastructure contractor with utility power-delivery exposure; validate margin quality and backlog mix before elevating.
WLDN is an underfollowed engineering/interconnection candidate after APG acquisition; verify whether APG creates material exposure to data-center substations and grid interconnection.

The investable bottleneck for this node is not only construction backlog but skilled labor availability, large-project execution margins, permitting cadence, and ability to convert MSAs/backlog into profitable revenue.

Potential future searches should examine electrical testing/commissioning, vegetation management, utility inspection, geospatial routing, and specialty line hardware separately; these were not fully covered in this 4-candidate pass.

node: Grid construction, specialty utility services, EPC execution, and skilled labor capacity
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-market universe around the hypothesis that grid buildout bottlenecks can migrate from equipment availability to qualified field labor, engineering, project management, utility contracting, substation execution, and interconnection services. The two-lane list uses Quanta Services as the obvious reference leader, then prioritizes mid/small-cap or less obvious execution-capacity names: MYR Group for electric T&D/substation construction, Primoris for utility power-delivery and critical infrastructure services, and Willdan for engineering, grid interconnection, substation design/construction-management exposure through APG. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
